quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon
questions.explanation: Stop signs are always octagon-shaped (eight sides). This shape is used only for stop signs.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road
Stop your car on the edge of the road
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking hard. Then carefully steer back onto the road. Watch for other traffic as you re-enter the road.

questions.question: What colors are highway exit distance signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Highway information signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs and alcohol together while driving?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone
It has no effect on your driving

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) affect your brain and driving ability. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes it much more dangerous and increases crash risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right
Hiking trails ahead and to the right
Hotel ahead and to the right
Hospital ahead and to the right

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: What traffic light comes after a steady yellow light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a red light is coming next.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow background and black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian
Stop and let the pedestrian cross

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross
questions.explanation: Always stop and let pedestrians cross safely. Be extra careful around children. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself
Steer firmly, slow down, and drive to a safe area to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, and drive to a safe area to stop
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need more force to steer. Reduce your speed and carefully drive to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit when getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Making it hard for you to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it hard for you to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how well you drive. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait and drive when you are calm and stable.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn the steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the car to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: If your car starts to skid, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. When the car straightens out, turn the steering wheel back the other way.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, they are signaling that they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this hand signal.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When the driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough room in front of your car to complete the pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they might not see you. For example, use your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as if they were thinking clearly.
Can drive faster because they are more alert.
Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: If you are worried, excited, crying, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Your emotions can distract you from driving. Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right of way.
Honk to warn drivers and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked cars. A person may step out of a parked car or from between parked cars. A driver in a parked car may not see you and might suddenly pull out.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When it is raining, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left just ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road marks where the road ends. If the line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Keeping your attention on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to your exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not make a sudden turn. Continue driving to the next exit instead.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop before the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic control signs or lights, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the same speed and go through.
Stop, look in all directions, then proceed.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be prepared to yield to avoid a crash. Slow down, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you finish the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that a red light is coming. If you see a yellow light, slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Being physically fit does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: Is failure to yield the right-of-way the leading cause of accidents in Nevada?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Right-of-way laws help traffic move safely through intersections. They promote courtesy and cooperation. Failure to yield the right-of-way is the leading cause of accidents in Nevada.

questions.question: If you see water covering the road, you should:

options.text: Drive until you think the water is too deep.
Drive through, as the water is unlikely to be too deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded roads. Turn around and find another way. You cannot tell how deep the water is or how fast it is moving. Your vehicle could be swept away or become submerged.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a busy intersection, and oncoming traffic blocks your view. You should:

options.text: Speed up when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you through.
Move slowly into each lane as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see in darkness. Other drivers' headlights can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Go, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection. You can proceed, but go slowly enough to stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person right away.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them wrongly can turn minor injuries into serious ones. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with a flashing signal, stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs of an oncoming train, such as a lowered crossing gate or the sound of a train.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Stops other cars from distracting you.
Gives you time to react to surprises.
Keeps traffic moving at safe speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: To have enough time to react to other drivers' mistakes, you must keep plenty of space between your vehicle and others.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The full width of a lane, like other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full width of a lane, like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the full lane width, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. You must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop first, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop first, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. After stopping, you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Using safe driving methods to prevent crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving methods to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe methods to prevent crashes. You adjust your speed and following distance based on weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad crossing gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give cyclists plenty of space when passing. Cyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too fast can force them off course.

questions.question: When should you drive slower than the posted speed limit?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: You must drive at a safe speed for the conditions. This means considering weather, visibility, road surface, road type, and traffic. You must slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road space.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road space.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, both vehicles need half the road space each. This gives both drivers room to pass safely.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Stop completely at every red eight-sided sign.

questions.question: When approaching a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must slow down and be ready to stop.
Must stop completely even if no traffic is near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down at a yield sign. Let pedestrians and traffic go first by stopping if needed. If it is safe, you may go without stopping.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
